chunks: Muḥammad ibn Sinān narrated from Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about the water of the valley, and he said:
Indeed, the Muslims are partners in water, fire, and pasture.

key_terms.النَّارِ: fire, as a basic communal utility
key_terms.الْكَلَإِ: pasture or herbage available for grazing
key_terms.الْمُسْلِمِينَ: the Muslims, the community addressed by the ruling
key_terms.الْوَادِي: the valley, referring to valley water
key_terms.شُرَكَاءُ: partners, meaning joint participants in a shared right
key_terms.مَاءِ: water, specifically as a resource under discussion

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about shared rights in water, fire, and pasture?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal principle concerning shared public resources. It indicates that water, fire, and pasture are common benefits in which Muslims share, highlighting communal rights over essential necessities.
